text: TSMC said on Thursday that personal data on some of its current and former employees was made available on an external website without authorization [1] . In a statement filed with the SEC and signed by chief financial officer Wendell Huang, the world's largest contract chipmaker said the information "has been verified to match data stored in the system services of a cloud service provider" [1] . TSMC said it has found no evidence that its own systems were compromised and that the data is unrelated to its operations or to customer information [1] . It is notifying affected staff and working with the cloud vendor, the relevant investigating authorities and an outside cybersecurity firm to establish what happened [1] . TSMC's statement does not name the cloud provider, say how many people were affected or list what data was exposed [1] . Wccftech, citing earlier reports in the Taiwanese press, said the leaked files cover roughly 46,000 employee records, include addresses, bank account numbers and emergency contact details, and that the hackers demanded three bitcoin and threatened to release the data if they were not paid [2] . TSMC has not confirmed those details. The disclosure comes in a busy week for the company: on Tuesday its board approved investments of up to $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI , and Taiwan's chip stocks fell on Thursday as Nvidia's CEO turmoil hit chipmakers .
